title: Polyhedra week: the declaration and four smaller entries
summary: On Mon 16 Nov at 18:35Z @oscillatory.net (274 followers) quote-posted an item titled "Smallest possible nopert polyhedra: the Septopert" with "it's polyhedra week"; @gracekind.net replied "let's get it trending", and the next day @norvid-studies.bsky.social wrote "it's polyhedra week now, lock in". The digest counts "polyhedra week" in 5 posts by 3 people and "polyhedron week" in 3 posts by 2 people. Besides the larger things (see the other made-poly... cards), members marked the week with smaller ones. @oszillate.bsky.social (75 followers) posted six photographs "from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™", each described in alt text: a woven dodecahedron sturdy enough that "you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested)", a rhombic dodecahedron from "a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property", and two designs of the poster's own. It has 38 likes. @anthonybecker.bsky.social posted a video titled "Glass Hour / for polyhedra week", music made "by an agent testing my music production harness". Under the "lock in" post, @shimmermathlabs.com wrote "the seasons change so quickly", @norvid-studies.bsky.social answered with an image captioned "the zonohedron in winter*" and a note that it was tool assisted, "but not well", and @shimmermathlabs.com replied with an eight-line poem about a pink tetrahedron, adding "(obviously tool assisted, i told it to write a love poem and it puts in math proofs)".

posts.text:
devouring time, eat through the plate
and fret the joints that turn my wrist.
your pink tetrahedron still fits
the little hollow of my fist.

your thumb wore one sharp vertex round
through proofs abandoned, lost, and found.
four points. i’ll make it sharp, and then
come think and wear it down again.

posts.text: Improptu posting some old stuff from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™, see descriptions in alt text
posts.alt:
Woven Dodecahedron, a classic model by David Brill of the British Origami Society; six strips that use one golden rectangle in its entirety. Maybe my favorite modular origami design. Unlike the average sort this is also *very* sturdy, you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested)

Also a model of Brill's, roughly an omnisunken rhombic hexecontahedron. Technically, not a polyhedron as much as a net / skeleton for one, ideally folded this would have zero volume.

The classic rhombic dodecahedron; unit design by Nick Robinson. I have a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property

Tiny "harlequin cube" showing the full symmetry elements of the octahedral group. Just six pieces that are mild variants of the classic Sonobe unit, much simpler than the finished model looks like.

A partially-sunken cube unit of my own design. Looks like 12 units but is actually just 6, each square face and its indents are one piece. I've wanted to use the principle from this to develop also the 24× sunken version similar to the previous cube, I never finished that project alas.

Another design of my own: kind of a half-unit for a sunken deltoidal icositetrahedron; this is one sheet, kind of a quadruple cootie catcher (though I suppose a smaller unit might make a sharper whole polyhedron). Also serves as a rosette for decorating gifts!
